patches.old: As solutes are reabsorbed, the luminal fluid becomes hypoosmotic, and water follows through **aquaporin-1 (AQP1)** channels on both apical and basolateral membranes.
patches.new: As solutes are reabsorbed, a very small osmotic gradient develops and water follows through **aquaporin-1 (AQP1)** channels on both apical and basolateral membranes, so the tubular fluid stays essentially isosmotic with plasma (~300 mOsm/kg) along the whole PCT.
patches.reason: Proximal reabsorption is isosmotic; luminal fluid does not become meaningfully hypoosmotic.

patches.old: Renal compensation for respiratory disorders takes 2–5 days to reach maximum effect, in contrast to the near-instantaneous respiratory compensation for metabolic disorders.
patches.new: Renal compensation for respiratory disorders takes about 2–5 days to reach maximum effect. Respiratory compensation for metabolic disorders is much faster: it begins within minutes, though it can take 12–24 hours to become maximal.
patches.reason: Respiratory compensation is fast but not instantaneous; maximal compensation takes 12–24 hours.

patches.old: A patient with uncontrolled diabetes mellitus presents with glucosuria despite normal blood glucose levels being only mildly elevated. Which mechanism best explains why glucose appears in the urine?
patches.new: A patient with uncontrolled diabetes mellitus has a plasma glucose of 300 mg/dL and glucose in the urine. Which mechanism best explains why glucose appears in the urine?
patches.reason: The original stem was self-contradictory ('normal' and 'mildly elevated').

patches.new: Choice C (150) comes from multiplying U by V but forgetting to divide by P. Choice D (300) comes from multiplying by P instead of dividing. Choice A does not follow from the clearance formula. Clearance calculations require all three variables.

visual.title: The nephron, segment by segment
visual.alt: Five panels in sequence. Proximal tubule: about 65 percent of sodium and water, NHE3 and SGLT2, always water permeable, targeted by acetazolamide and SGLT2 inhibitors. Thin descending limb: water only via AQP1. Thick ascending limb: about 25 percent of sodium via NKCC2, never water permeable, targeted by loop diuretics. Distal tubule: about 5 percent via NCC with PTH-regulated calcium reabsorption, water impermeable, targeted by thiazides. Collecting duct: 2 to 5 percent via ENaC under aldosterone, water only with ADH via AQP2, targeted by spironolactone and amiloride. A note traces tubular fluid osmolality.
visual.caption: Typical textbook shares; they shift with volume status and hormones.
